reading.body:
All five data centers recorded for Ohio in this dataset are located in New Albany, operated by two companies, Quality Technology Services and Vantage, within a tight geographic cluster.

The coordinates confirm that these are not merely the same city but effectively the same corridor, with QTS running two facilities and Vantage running three within a narrow band of latitude and longitude. That kind of density is characteristic of a campus build-out strategy, where operators co-locate successive buildings to share infrastructure, fiber, and power interconnections rather than distributing risk across a wider geography.

For AI workloads, geographic concentration cuts both ways. A single power or cooling failure, or a constrained substation, can affect every facility in the cluster simultaneously. The dataset does not include megawatt capacity figures, so no inference about total power draw or available headroom is possible. The record also covers only five facilities and makes no claim to be an exhaustive survey of Ohio data center activity.
